# Observability-as-a-Service — Observability + Fundi Tenancy Model

**OaaS is not a separate node.** It is the tenancy and commercialisation model layered on top of the **observability** and **fundi** collections (the core guarantee nodes for sensing and self-healing in the Mzizi DNA helix). The four tables that implement it are live in `public` schema and remain canonical post-4.1.x.

## The four tables

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `observability_domains` | Tenant registry. Each row is one domain consuming OaaS — internally, free, pro, or enterprise tier. |
| `observability_events` | Structural event sink. Renders, errors, chaos injections, healing events, health checks. **Never stores PII** — enforced by a CHECK constraint that rejects metadata containing user, email, name, token, password, session, cookie, auth, ip, phone, address, or dob keys. |
| `fundi_issues` | Failure reports surfaced from observability. Each issue carries a severity, error type, blast radius, diagnostic source, and healing plan. Status moves through `open → triaging → healing → awaiting_review → resolved` (or `wont_fix`). |
| `fundi_healing_log` | Append-only audit trail of healing actions. Logged once, never updated, never deleted by authenticated clients. |

## Tenancy tiers

The `tier` column on `observability_domains` is a CHECK-constrained enum:

| Tier | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `internal` | Nyuchi-owned domain consuming OaaS internally. No commercial commitment. |
| `free` | External tenant on the free tier. Limited rate, no chaos injection. |
| `pro` | External tenant on the pro tier. Higher rate, basic chaos and analytics. |
| `enterprise` | External tenant on the enterprise tier. Full chaos, full analytics, dedicated support. |

Feature flags per tenant — `portal_links_enabled`, `chaos_enabled`, `fundi_enabled`, `analytics_enabled` — are stored on the same row. Rate is bounded by `max_chaos_injections_per_hour` and `health_check_interval_seconds`.

## Why OaaS sits on observability + fundi, not as its own node

The **observability** node does the watching (assurance + the event streams). The **fundi** node does the healing. OaaS is the *commercial framing* of those two capabilities — the multi-tenancy registry, the tier gating, the rate limiting, the per-tenant configuration. It is not a new behaviour; it is a packaging of two existing behaviours.

If OaaS were its own node it would force a re-explanation of the DNA helix. The helix already classifies both observability and fundi as **mzizi core** (the fixed guarantee). OaaS commercialises that guarantee without changing it.

## The data flow

1. An observability-node component detects a failure or runs a probe.
2. It writes to `observability_events` (the structural fact) via `emit_observability(...)` and to `fundi_issues` (the actionable report) via `emit_issue(...)`.
3. Fundi reads `fundi_issues`, opens a GitHub issue, executes its healing plan, and logs each step to `fundi_healing_log` via `emit_healing(...)`.
4. The tenant's `observability_domains` row gates whether any of this happens at all and at what intensity.

## Privacy guarantees

The `observability_events.metadata` CHECK constraint is the doctrinal teeth. It rejects any JSONB metadata containing keys named `user`, `email`, `name`, `token`, `password`, `session`, `cookie`, `auth`, `ip`, `phone`, `address`, or `dob`. There is no way to write PII to this table without dropping the constraint. The constraint is the doctrine, encoded.

The ±5-minute timestamp gate on every event table (the `created_at` / `executed_at` RLS check) prevents backdating and future-dating. This is enforced in the schema, not in code — the database refuses to accept an out-of-window event regardless of the client. Open infrastructure: integrity guaranteed by the substrate, not by trust.

Fundi issues may contain operational diagnostic data but never user identifiers. Healing actions are logged with `approved_by` (a system or human actor) but never with end-user identity.

## Future commercial work

A later FRD will surface OaaS publicly — pricing pages, tenant onboarding UI, dashboards for each tier. That work is queued; this page documents the substrate that already exists.
